• Liquid biopsy (ctDNA)
• Digital pathology (AI-assisted)

Molecular Pathologist / Molecular Diagnostics Laboratory – Performs biomarker testing, genomic profiling, and molecular analysis to identify actionable mutations and guide precision treatment decisions.

Medical Oncologist – Interprets molecular profiling, pathology, and imaging findings to determine personalized treatment strategies, including targeted therapy, immunotherapy, chemotherapy, and follow-up

Interventional Radiologist - Performs CT-guided percutaneous biopsy.

Pathologist - Evaluates tissue samples and characterizes the type of lung cancer.

Lung cancer survivors carry an elevated, sustained risk of second primary lung cancer (approx. 0.7-1.1% per patient per year, cumulative over time with no plateau) and recurrence, yet most centers apply a uniform, fixed-interval CT surveillance schedule (e.g., every 6-12 months for 2 years) rather than tailoring frequency and duration to each patient's actual risk.

https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S155608642400683X
column5:
AI/deep-learning risk-stratified postoperative surveillance: Models trained on pre- and post-operative chest CT imaging biomarkers predict individual risk of recurrence or new primary lung cancer, enabling personalized surveillance intervals (more frequent imaging for higher-risk survivors, less frequent/lower-burden follow-up for lower-risk survivors) instead of one-size-fits-all schedules.

https://www.jacr.org/article/S1546-1440(25)00466-1/fulltext
